Dense adjacency and differentiable pooling

Source: R/pooling.R
to_dense_adj.Rd

to_dense_adj() turns a batched edge_index into a B by L by L tensor, L the largest graph, with adj[b, i, j] the weight of the edge from local node j to local node i of graph b (rows are targets, so adj %*% x aggregates incoming messages). Repeated edges add up.

Usage

to_dense_adj(edge_index, batch, edge_weight = NULL)

dense_diff_pool(x, adj, s, mask = NULL)

dense_graph_conv(in_features, out_features, normalize = TRUE)

Arguments

edge_index

Long tensor, 2 by E, 1-based.

batch

Graph membership of each node (R vector or tensor).

edge_weight

Optional edge weights.

x

Dense node features, B by L by F.

adj

Dense adjacency, B by L by L.

s

Assignment logits, B by L by C.

mask

Logical B by L tensor of real (non padding) nodes.

in_features, out_features

Feature sizes.

normalize

Divide aggregated messages by the weighted in degree.

Value

to_dense_adj(): a tensor. dense_diff_pool(): a list with x, adj, s (the softmax assignment), link_loss and entropy_loss.

Details

dense_diff_pool() is the DiffPool operator (Ying et al. 2018). With assignment logits s (B by L by C), \(S = \mathrm{softmax}(s)\) over clusters, padding rows set to zero, $$X' = S^\top X,\quad A' = S^\top A S,$$ the auxiliary link loss \(\lVert A - S S^\top \rVert_F / (B L^2)\) and entropy loss \(\mathrm{mean}_i(-\sum_c S_{ic} \log S_{ic})\).

dense_graph_conv() is \(W_1 \tilde A X + W_2 X\) on dense batches, \(\tilde A\) row normalized when normalize = TRUE; it is the GNN used on coarsened graphs.

Memory is \(O(B L^2)\), so these suit batches of small graphs.

References

Ying, You, Morris, Ren, Hamilton and Leskovec (2018) Hierarchical graph representation learning with differentiable pooling.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  b <- graph_batch(dataset_synthetic_graphs(3, seed = 1))
  tt <- graph_tensors(b)
  adj <- to_dense_adj(tt$edge_index, b$batch)
  d <- to_dense_batch(tt$x, b$batch)
  pooled <- dense_diff_pool(d$x, adj, torch::torch_randn(3, d$L, 2), d$mask)
  dim(pooled$adj)
}
#> [1] 3 2 2
